archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (defense-first)
archetype.definition: Tampa Bay grades as a top-ten team by net efficiency and has outscored opponents, but a bottom-tier passing game and a string of close losses have it sitting last in a four-way tie at the top of the NFC South.

report.headline: A top-two defense dragged to 3-6 by a broken passing game and coin flips.
report.take:
This is a strange Buccaneers team, and a new one. Todd Bowles has a defense that ranks second in EPA allowed per play, against both the pass and the run. That is a sharp break from last year, when the unit sat 16th. The offense has gone the other way. It ranks 29th in EPA and 30th passing, and it has leaned on the run, with a pass rate 7.5 points under expectation. The result is a team with a positive point differential, a net EPA that ranks 10th, and a 3-6 record.

The gap between the play and the record is mostly close games. Tampa has won 14.3% of its one-score games, 30th in the league, and every one of its six losses has been close. The differential implies 3.9 wins, so the raw luck is modest. The bigger story is that an offense this poor through the air can't close: it sacks itself out of drives at a 9.2% rate and carries 14 turnovers. The quarterback shuffle didn't help. Jalon Daniels started weeks 4 through 6 before Baker Mayfield came back, and neither has made the passing game work.

The numbers hide two things. The defense's EPA is helped by a league-leading 20 takeaways, including 13 over the last three games, and that pace will cool. But the base is real: a 40.3% success rate allowed (3rd) and the third-best EPA against short passes say this unit wins snaps, not just coin flips. Its flaws are structural rather than lucky. It barely pressures the quarterback (30th in pressure rate), it misses tackles (29th), and it gives up real value deep (20th). Offensively, the run game is a genuine asset: 4.81 yards a carry (3rd) and the third-most time of possession. The recent box scores, though, show how lopsided it has become, with 64 passing yards in the Carolina rout and zero against Atlanta.

Where it's heading is better than the standings suggest. Seven of the last eight games come against teams at .500 or worse, four of them in a division where nobody is above 3-5. A defense this good and a run game this efficient should win more close games than 14.3%. Takeaway regression will bite, though, and the ceiling stays capped until Mayfield's passing gets back toward league average.

strengths.title: Elite down-to-down defense
strengths.body: Tampa ranks second in EPA allowed overall, passing and rushing, and third in success rate allowed, so this goes beyond turnovers. The coverage underneath is the engine: it ranks third against short passes and has erased opposing WR1s, ranking first in EPA per target against them. With pressure this low, it is winning on structure and coverage, which tends to hold up better than sack-driven defense.

strengths.title: League-best ball hawks
strengths.body: The defense leads the league with 20 takeaways and has a +7 turnover margin, despite the offense's giveaways. The recent surge, including five against Chicago, is the part that won't last; takeaway rates swing wildly. Expect fewer short fields and fewer gift possessions going forward, even if the defense keeps playing well.

strengths.title: Efficient, clock-eating run game
strengths.body: The line is creating real room: 4.81 yards a carry ranks third, run EPA ranks eighth, and yards before contact ranks ninth. Bucky Irving carries the load with Kenny Gainwell behind him. Together with the defense, the run game produces the third-highest time of possession, which shortens games and protects a shaky passing attack.

concerns.title: The passing game is broken
concerns.body: Pass EPA ranks 30th, and the sack rate allowed of 9.2% ranks 29th. Time to throw is not short, so the sacks look shared between protection and quarterbacks holding the ball. This is the real flaw on the roster rather than noise. It has persisted through both Mayfield and Daniels, and it is why the offense can't finish close games.

concerns.title: No pass rush, loose tackling
concerns.body: Tampa ranks 30th in pressure rate and 29th in missed-tackle rate. Good quarterbacks with time can find the deep ball, where the defense ranks only 20th. The coverage has masked this so far, but it is the vulnerability that elite offenses will test.

concerns.title: Can't close one-score games
concerns.body: A 14.3% win rate in one-score games ranks 30th, and the record trails the point differential. Some of that is variance that should even out. Some of it is the passing game failing in exactly the moments when a team has to throw, so expect only partial correction.

trend.note: After a 1-5 start full of close losses, the defense took over: a 43-13 rout at Carolina, a 16-0 shutout of Atlanta and a narrow cover at Chicago with five takeaways. The passing game has not improved alongside it.

nextGame.headline: Best defense by EPA meets a top-seven offense in a dome
nextGame.body:
Tampa comes off the bye to face a 6-2 Detroit team built nearly the opposite way. The Lions have the seventh-best offense by EPA, fourth passing, and a defense that ranks 30th. The marquee matchup is the Bucs' coverage against Jared Goff behind a line that allows little pressure (fifth). That favors Detroit, because Tampa's rush can't speed him up. On the other side, Detroit's weakness is pass defense, 27th in EPA. Tampa is poorly built to exploit that, but the Lions do sack the quarterback (27, second in the league), which hits the Bucs' biggest offensive flaw. Detroit has also won 80% of its one-score games. No line was posted in the dossier.

Availability leans slightly toward Tampa. Detroit has linebacker Jack Campbell on IR, and he played 97% of snaps. Cornerback D.J. Reed, safety Kerby Joseph, linebacker DJ Wonnum and center Cade Mays were all listed out, with return estimates before this game that aren't guaranteed. Tampa's key question is safety Antoine Winfield Jr., questionable with the ankle that knocked him out at Chicago. Linebacker Yaya Diaby (MCL) is projected back around kickoff. Receiver Jalen McMillan is on IR and isn't expected back right away. The bye gives Tampa 14 days of rest.

waysToWin.title: Run it and shrink the game
waysToWin.body: Tampa's run game ranks third in yards per carry, and Detroit's run defense is only mid-pack, now without Campbell in the middle. Long, clock-heavy drives keep Goff on the sideline and play to the Bucs' time-of-possession edge. A low-possession game is the one Tampa wants.

waysToWin.title: Cade Otton against a leaky TE defense
waysToWin.body: Detroit ranks 31st in both points over average and EPA per target allowed to tight ends, and opponents throw to the position more than the league norm against them. Otton is tied for the second-most targets on the team. Quick, safe throws to the tight end are the cleanest way for a struggling passing game to move the chains without taking sacks.

waysToWin.title: Win the turnover battle again
waysToWin.body: Tampa leads the league in takeaways, and Detroit's defense ranks 25th in forcing them. Even a modest edge here, with short fields, could swing a game the Bucs otherwise trail on talent at the quarterback spot.

waysToLose.title: Sacks kill drives
waysToLose.body: Detroit's 27 sacks rank second, and Tampa's 9.2% sack rate allowed ranks 29th. If the Bucs fall behind schedule and have to throw on third down, drives will stall and the run-first plan collapses.

waysToLose.title: Goff gets time and goes deep
waysToLose.body: Tampa's pass rush ranks 30th in pressure rate, and Detroit's line allows the fifth-lowest pressure. That gives a fourth-ranked passing offense a clean pocket against a defense that is only 20th on deep balls. If Winfield sits, the back end loses its most-used piece.

waysToLose.title: Another close loss
waysToLose.body: Tampa wins 14.3% of its one-score games; Detroit wins 80% and goes for it on fourth down at the league's highest rate. A tight fourth quarter favors the team that can pass and the coach who stays aggressive.

nextGame.watch: Tampa's early-down run success: if Irving keeps the Bucs in third-and-short, Detroit's pass rush never gets its matchup.

restOfSeason.body:
The schedule is the best thing Tampa has going. After Detroit, six of the last seven opponents are at .500 or worse, including a winless Chargers team and four division games against teams with three wins. The defense's success rate and short-pass coverage look sustainable. The 13 takeaways over the last three weeks do not, so points allowed should drift up a little even as the defense keeps grading well. The one-score record should also improve, simply because it can hardly get worse, and that is the most likely path to more wins.

What won't fix itself is the passing game. Until the sack rate and pass EPA move toward the middle of the league, Tampa will keep playing low-scoring games decided late. A team that wins with defense and the run can take a division this flat, but it will look shaky doing it.
swingFactors: Whether Mayfield's passing climbs toward league average
How fast the takeaway rate regresses
Close-game results in four division games

confidence.note: Nine games, a QB switch, and a takeaway-boosted defense.
